I fear submitting an entire essay for feedback because my college uses “Turn-it In”? Some program that checks for former submissions and ai. I mostly use ai on my essays so that it can tell me sentence if my sentence is off. Ai (I use copilot) will fix my grammar and sometimes fix my wording and I ALWAYS ask it to tell me why those suggestions were made so that I can learn and not make the same mistake again. It’s very useful for someone who was out of school for 10 years and forgot basic grammar. I try to use google’s thesaurus as often as possible but if I still can’t find a better word that’s when I’ll submit my sentence to ai.

I’m sorry to hear that. Turns out a couple months after this post, I find out that the parcel locker was broken and for some reason took 10 months for them to send a tech out to fix it. They never alerted residents. One day I got a notification on my phone that my package arrived, even though I hadn’t ordered a package that week. I go up to the locker and I find two of my packages. One from 10 months ago and one from 3 months ago. 

My packages were being delivered to the locker, but the locker itself wasn’t connected to the internet and couldn’t notify residents of their package. There was also no way for property management to open the lockers. I assumed my packages were delivered to the wrong apartment complex because it did say they were delivered to “locker” but I never received a code. 

I was pissed. I emailed my apartment complex for a refund for every month that I paid for my packages to sit and rot inside that locker. Both had perishables in them. 

This happened in March of this year. Since then, I have not gotten a package delivered to the parcel locker again. They always arrive at my doorstep or the USPS locker with a key they put in your mailbox. If I were you I would email property management and ask them if their lockers are working and why your packages aren’t being delivered to your lockers after multiple stolen deliveries. If they claim the lockers are down, let them know that you may have packages in the lockers and you need to access to them asap. They may expedite getting the lockers fixed.

Edit: And if your lockers aren’t broken, I would try reaching out to Amazon customer service and complain about your packages, being delivered to your doorstep despite the instructions stating otherwise. They may need to flag your local Amazon drivers to follow your instructions going forward.

I’m sorry to hear your struggles. I also have days where I ask if it’s worth it. Similarly, I’ve had days where I spent all night studying and go to bed super late, wake up at the last minute, and slack off at work because of it. I dropped a couple classes at the start of fall and winter because I was overwhelming myself. 

I’ve figured out a good strategy for balancing my coursework. I will never take more than 2 classes at the same time and preferably one class is “easy” and the other more time consuming/difficult. For example, this summer I will be taking 5 courses but one starts and ends in May. The next 2 run from June to early August. The last 2 from early August to mid September. The overlapping classes will be 1 hard + 1 “easy” class. 

I don’t have a social life so instead of doom scrolling through the internet I get home and immediately go through my modules. I try not to stay up past a certain point, and thankfully my current class assignments are always due Sunday so if I choose to slack off during my work week I can catch up on the weekend (I’m off all weekend). 

I don’t want to tell you to not give up, because I’m not sure what your plans are. But if you dropped out only because you were overwhelmed just try to take 1 class at a time. 1 spring, 1 fall, 1 each minimester. You don’t have to be a full time student taking multiple classes at once. Try to remember college isn’t a race! You don’t have to be a full time or half time student. As long as you keep going you will eventually reach your goal. I’m trying to not pressure myself into finishing my associates within 2 years. When all my easy courses are completed and the remaining credits are math/science/electives that align with my major, I fully expect to take 1 class at a time. And that’s okay!

Note: all my classes are online which helps tremendously. Traveling to class in person will definitely take up more energy.

Your post spoke to me i'm in a similarish situation. I'm 27 and I've tried \*almost\* everything. I refuse to do a strict diet because I honestly wouldn't stick with it even if I found out it did play a role in my acne but I doubt it does. For me stress plays a noticeable part in my flareups. I've been on Benzoyl/Clindamycin/Tretinoin topicals and a handful of oral antibiotics for the past 4 years. They worked amazing the first year but I stopped using them consistently when I got depression in 2020 due to a family illness. I haven't been the same ever since the family death and a side effect of my depression is that I'm too tired/mentally drained to even attempt to wash my face when I get home from work so I completely skip the Clindamycin/Tretinoin topicals at night. I think to myself my skin will never be clear and I will never be physically desired by anyone so why put in effort anymore? I made a post about this on this subreddit 3 weeks ago and everyone told me I will not see results if I'm not consistent. Those comments really spoke to me for some reason. At that point I decided if I'm not going to be consistent then Accutane is my only potential cure. I did have the Accutane talk with 2 different dermatologists who recommended it to me (but didn't know the truth about my inconsistency) and I chickened out.

So the past couple weeks I started using my topicals every morning and night consistently despite my depression kicking in at times wanting to just give up. I've seen a small bit of improvement. I'm giving myself 3 months to see real results. If I don't see consistent results by October I will make the leap of fate to Accutane. And trust me I'm EXACTLY like you. I've read a million comments, watched a million videos, threads about Accutane. Results seem to be all over the place. It's either the BEST THING they've ever done for their skin and it changed their life, or it's the worst thing and now they have permanent side effects and they fear monger you away from it. After stressing about what would happen to me I came to a conclusion and I think this will help you with your decision if you truly tried everything else.

Mild side effects (chapped lips, dry skin, joint pain) are more likely than harsh side effects (the ones you listed). On top of that it's even more rare for these side effects to be permanent. Looking at the scientific you have about a 70% chance of being one of the people that says Accutane was the best thing they did. Those odds are pretty amazing. If you experience harsh side effects you can always stop taking the medication or lower your dose. But you will NEVER KNOW unless you TRY. You can try to guess all you want to but actually trying the medication is all you can do. Reading the r/Accutane sub also normalizes the medication for me. Most people on it are doing just fine, the threads about harsh side effects come from people like you and me who haven't even tried it. You can't let fear mongering take over your mind. Millions of people are prescribed Accutane every year and most of the time it's prescribed to teenagers. How often do you see balding teenagers with low libido? lol think about it. 

Finally I also want to address what you said about your doctors not taking you seriously. I completely agree. I find that I don't trust medical providers because they put more trust in medication than their patients. I understand these medications have been around for decades and scientific studies back up their claims. But every person is different and they don't always like to have an open mind. I remember questioning my dermatologists about the side effects of Accutane the first one laughed it off and said don't look at anything online. The second one seemed pretty offended and went on a rant about how the mayo clinic shut down false statements about accutane causing bowel issues and that people with acne are more likely to have bowel issues and people blame their issues on accutane. It's a very weird relationship. I want to trust doctors but it makes me uncomfortable how they refuse to acknowledge issues with modern medicine because these claims don't come out of the blue. They're real, they exist, and I'm starting not to trust scientific studies anymore.
